questions.stem: What is the correct order of biological organisation from smallest to largest?

options.text: Organ, tissue, cell, organ system, organism
Tissue, cell, organ, organism, organ system
Cell, organ, tissue, organ system, organism
Cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism

questions.explanation: The correct hierarchy is: cell, tissue, organ, organ system, organism. Each level is built from the previous one.

options.text: A complete living organism
A group of similar cells working together to perform a specific function
A single specialised cell
A group of different organs working together

questions.explanation: A tissue is a group of similar cells that work together to carry out a particular function. For example, muscle tissue is made up of muscle cells.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of an organ?

options.text: Muscle tissue
A red blood cell
The heart
The circulatory system

questions.explanation: The heart is an organ because it is made up of different tissues (muscle tissue, connective tissue, nerve tissue) working together to perform the function of pumping blood.

options.text: A group of organs working together to perform a particular function
A collection of tissues inside one organ
All the cells in the body
A single organ that performs multiple functions

questions.explanation: An organ system is a group of organs that work together to carry out a particular function. For example, the digestive system includes the stomach, intestines, and liver.

questions.stem: Which is an example of epithelial tissue?

options.text: A neurone
Bicep muscle
The lining of the intestine
A tendon

questions.explanation: Epithelial tissue covers body surfaces and lines organs. The lining of the intestine is an example of epithelial tissue that aids in absorption.

questions.stem: The digestive system is an example of:

options.text: An organ system
An organ
A cell
A tissue

questions.explanation: The digestive system is an organ system because it consists of multiple organs (mouth, oesophagus, stomach, intestines, liver, pancreas) working together to digest food.

questions.stem: What makes an organ different from a tissue?

options.text: An organ is smaller than a tissue
An organ can only be found in animals
An organ is made up of one type of cell
An organ contains different types of tissues working together

questions.explanation: An organ is made up of different types of tissues that work together to perform a specific function, whereas a tissue is made up of similar cells performing the same function.
